mechanism.description: Gwendolyn Vance exploited cognitive bias in memory anchoring by using a rehearsed choreographic cue combined with a deliberately staged gramophone silent intermission of exactly seven minutes. Witnesses anchored their memories on her last pose and the music, believing she was immobile in the rehearsal room during the murder. Meanwhile, Gwendolyn slipped to Bertram’s cabin during the silent pause, struck him with the heavy baton, and returned before the music restarted, using a concealed crew corridor to avoid detection. The gramophone’s winding mechanism was remotely triggered and manipulated to create a false timeline, tricking observers about the time of death and Gwendolyn's location.

steps.observation: The gramophone log on the rehearsal board shows music paused exactly at four o'clock for a silent seven-minute intermission.
Witnesses describe Gwendolyn holding the last dance pose unusually long during the silent intermission, with her voice heard from the rehearsal room.
Maintenance logs and a janitor’s report indicate a crew corridor door was temporarily unlocked and later found with a missing master key.
Close inspection of the gramophone shows fresh winding marks and wear on the spring mechanism, inconsistent with normal playback.
Forensic examination indicates the actual time of death as a quarter past four, outside the apparent time of death at four o'clock fixed by the gramophone’s silent pause.
